newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnair says plans structural changes. [CORRECTED 12:02 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Finnair says plans structural changes. [CORRECTED 12:02 GMT]

text.p: Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy on Friday said it planned structural measures to boost its profitability, but gave no details.

"We at Finnair have set the goal of achieving structural changes to reduce cost levels and increase revenues so that the group's ability to make profits will improve by a yearly level of about 500 million markka by the start of the next millenium," CEO Antti Potila said in a statement with the group's first-half results.
(Corrects from "...from the current yearly level of 500 million markka...")
"The company has undertaken many new measures to improve profitability. Efforts will concentrate on cost cuts and higher efficiency," the company said.
"We can't afford to wait... because costs outstrip revenue. Action must be taken," Potila said. "We have to strike a balance between income and expenditure."
Finnair said its first-half pre-tax profits had fallen almost 50 percent to 233.5 million markka from 463.0 million in the year-ago period.
In addition to a 22 percent rise in jet fuel prices Finnair said personnel and other flight service costs rose as well.
"The personnel costs for flight operations rose by 10 percent, traffic charges 5.0 percent, ground handling charges 10 percent and passenger service charges 19 percent," it said.
